comment:
Two source-backed issues affect the new unattended receiver at `43aff5ce`.

**Verified by source inspection:** the helper wires explicit on/off commands to the user unit, the panel queries its active state, and the migration adds `bluez-obex`. Real transfers and UI behavior were not tested.

## The receiver does not enforce the advertised paired-only restriction

The [new unit](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/43aff5ceff663e5558c86394842db885cd226ad5/default/systemd/user/omarchy-bluetooth-files.service#L14-L19) uses `bt-obex --auto-accept`. BlueZ 5.87's [Object Push defaults](https://github.com/bluez/bluez/blob/5.87/src/profile.c#L2152-L2161) use `BT_IO_SEC_LOW` and disable service authorization; obexd's [profile registration](https://github.com/bluez/bluez/blob/5.87/obexd/plugins/bluetooth.c#L222-L276) does not override those settings. The packaged [bt-obex agent](https://github.com/khvzak/bluez-tools/blob/7cb788c9c43facfd2d14ff50e16d6a19f033a6a7/src/lib/obex_agent.c#L206-L246) auto-accepts without checking the sender's pairing state.

```text
Inspected acceptance path, not an on-air reproduction:
OPP connection -> no service-authorization gate
               -> bt-obex auto-accept -> incoming file
                  (no paired-device check)
```

**Impact:** opting in can permit an unpaired nearby sender that can reach the adapter to submit files. Android's bonded-device picker constrains that client, not other OBEX senders. Discoverability and knowledge of the adapter address affect reachability; no hardware exploit was reproduced. Enabling the unit also preserves this opt-in across later logins.

**Suggested change:** enforce the paired-only policy using verified sender identity at the receiver's authorization decision, or choose a receiver that provides that protection. Remove the paired-only guarantee from the comments and UI/documentation until it is enforced.

## Receiving a duplicate filename can overwrite an existing download

The selected `bt-obex` implementation [retains the incoming name](https://github.com/khvzak/bluez-tools/blob/7cb788c9c43facfd2d14ff50e16d6a19f033a6a7/src/bt-obex.c#L362-L375), then [calls `g_rename` on completion](https://github.com/khvzak/bluez-tools/blob/7cb788c9c43facfd2d14ff50e16d6a19f033a6a7/src/bt-obex.c#L165-L182) without a no-replace check or checking its result.

```text
Source-derived example, same filesystem:
incoming report.pdf -> rename into Downloads/report.pdf
                       existing report.pdf is replaced
```

**Impact:** even a legitimately paired sender can silently replace an existing download. Enforcing pairing alone would not fix this.

**Suggested change:** use a collision-safe destination handoff, such as unique names with atomic no-replace semantics, and check the final move result. Avoid unattended delivery through the unmodified clobbering path.
